author: potuz
content: <@425572898787426305> by removing payments I mean the very simple idea of selecting builders from the builder set at random weighted by their stake. And deleting completely everything about trustless payments

author: m.kalinin
content: oh, i see, that sounds like a big change

author: potuz
content: Oh not really, it's a simplifying one

author: potuz
content: You just remove stuff mostly and add a lookahead for builders. And can even give them negative issuance. It's a big change from the staking market perspective but from the specs/implementation point of view it's a simplifying one

author: m.kalinin
content: it is definitely a simplification of the protocol. changing the market sounds big and hard to champion

author: potuz
content: Otoh it means going back to the status quo: stakers can allocate to the builder slice and sell JIT with mev boost. The drop in issuance is IMO the only thing that is hard to get through

author: m.kalinin
content:
> stakers can allocate to the builder slice and sell JIT with mev boost

Do you mean they sell via protocol only when favorable builder is selected and use mev boost otherwise?

author: potuz
content: no, I mean sell via MEV boost exactly as it is today, off protocol. The point is that attesters (home stakers) do not need to be worried anymore about MEV and about proposing. And large pools can just take a percentage of their stake (say suppose today 15% of their income comes from proposals and 85% from attestations) then they'll move 15% of their stake to the builder slice and sell via Mev Boost exactly as today and they'll keep the status quo. If in addition we charge them (giving negative issuance to builders) then the computation is modified accordingly.
